page: Microsoft Azure D32_v3 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dv3 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8171M processor with an x86_64 architecture, providing 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 16 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The CPU operates at a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz and is equipped with 32 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 35 MB L3 cache. The hardware configuration includes 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core, alongside a bundled 819 GB local SSD for storage.

Performance benchmarks indicate a distinct tradeoff between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is relatively weak, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 10% and 25% respectively. Similarly, single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression are positioned in the bottom 25%. However, the server leverages its 32 vCPUs to achieve average multi-core and multi-threaded performance. Multi-core stress-ng, Geekbench multi-core, and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression all register in the middle 50% of benchmarked systems.

Memory and storage operations align with the middle tier of performance. The system achieves average memory bandwidth, reaching 1207.38 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 100.75 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Database operations, Redis SET operations at 20.47 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput at 17.6 GB/sec also fall within the average range. For machine learning workloads, the server handles prompt processing and text generation for small and medium LLM models at average speeds, though prompt processing for large models drops to a poor 3.73 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D32_v3 offers a balanced resource density of compute, memory, and local SSD storage without the premium of specialized hardware. It is best suited for workloads that benefit from multi-threaded execution rather than raw single-core speed, such as general-purpose web serving, relational databases, software compilation, and medium-scale data processing.
